interest: This document is of interest to diplomatic and economic historians because it illustrates the global reach of U.S. diplomatic intelligence, showing how an American embassy in Europe (Paris) reported on Japanese resource investments in South America. It highlights Japan's interwar quest for energy independence and alternative petroleum resources—specifically shale oil in Lonquimay, Chile—long before the Pacific War, reflecting early international awareness of Japanese strategic capital penetration in Latin America.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet under decimal classification 894.503125, which covers the investment of Japanese capital in Chile. The sheet records Despatch No. 3296 dated January 30, 1933, from the U.S. Embassy in France under Ambassador Walter E. Edge, concerning Japanese participation in the exploitation of shale petroleum fields at Lonquimay, Chile. It serves as an administrative register reflecting interwar diplomatic surveillance of Japanese efforts to secure strategic petroleum assets in Latin America.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers recording a despatch from U.S. Ambassador to France Walter E. Edge regarding Japanese investment in Chilean shale petroleum deposits at Lonquimay.
subfiles.summary: This administrative 'List of Papers' docket sheet catalogs Despatch No. 3296 sent on January 30, 1933, by U.S. Ambassador to France Walter E. Edge to the Department of State. The recorded paper concerns Japanese participation in developing the shale petroleum fields located at Lonquimay, Chile. The sheet captures State Department indexing of foreign economic intelligence tracking Japanese capital ventures in strategic resource sectors in South America.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Japanese Participation in Lonquimay Shale Petroleum Fields
